annotation.title_clean: Ethical concerns in rescue robotics: a scoping review
annotation.title_en: Ethical concerns in rescue robotics: a scoping review
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Battistuzzi, L.; Recchiuto, C.T.; Sgorbissa, A.
annotation.summary_en: Scoping review of academic literature on ethics of rescue/disaster robots. Of 429 papers screened, six qualified. Seven themes emerged: fairness and discrimination, false expectations, labor replacement, privacy, responsibility, safety, trust. The literature is scant and disparate, but the papers endorse a proactive approach to ethical concerns.
key_provisions_or_claims: Only six of 429 papers met criteria; literature on rescue robot ethics is scant and disparate.
Seven themes: fairness/discrimination, false expectations, labor replacement, privacy, responsibility, safety, trust.
Fairness and discrimination is the most discussed concern (4/6 papers), e.g., victim prioritisation by robots.
Papers uniformly endorse proactive handling of ethical concerns before rescue robots become ubiquitous.
Most studies use simulations or scenarios; only one tested an ethical framework in actual deployment.
